DCI.text: Distributor of IT hardware, networking and cybersecurity products. Demand is strong: ==products revenue +40%== and ==security software +29%== in Q2. Oct–Dec is the ==festive and year-end IT buying season==, which usually lifts distributor volumes. Watch: the business needs more working capital (borrowings up to ₹123 cr, inventory up), so higher interest cost can eat into profit.

MODIS.text: Real-estate redevelopment developer. ==Bookings ₹202 cr in H1 vs ₹54 cr== a year ago, at ==8% higher average price== per sq ft. ==₹156 cr of sold flats is still to be booked as revenue==, and two projects are near completion (==Rashmi Square 80% built==, Rashmi Signature 62%), so revenue recognition should rise. A new redevelopment project was added, and ₹505 cr of unsold flats is future potential. Watch: two big projects (Icon, Avenue) are still early-stage.

PANACHE.text: Supplies IT hardware, including laptops. ==New ₹51.4 cr laptop order== from an IT-sector customer (2 Nov 2026), to be delivered ==within about 30 days==: more than 60% of last quarter's sales, falling fully in Oct–Dec. Repeat large orders from corporate and IT customers are driving demand. Watch: orders are lumpy and the customer is not named.

526433.text: Engineering and product R&D services company with design centres in India and abroad (USA, UK, Singapore, Japan, Mexico). Demand from overseas clients is scaling fast: ==quarterly sales jumped from ₹199 cr to ₹268 cr in one quarter==. Next quarter is compared with a ==weak Dec 2025 quarter==, so high growth is likely. No specific order or capacity news found. Watch: promoter holding fell from 57.4% to 53.5% in October.

530477.text: Makes pharma excipients (co-polymers used in tablet coatings and formulations) for domestic and export pharma companies: steady, repeat demand. Sales have risen for 3 quarters in a row, to a ==record ₹44 cr==. No new capacity or big orders announced, so growth depends on pharma volumes and export demand continuing. Margins stay high because raw-material costs have been stable.

544406.text: IT-infrastructure, cybersecurity and managed-services provider. ==Added 10+ large enterprise clients== (Sun Pharma, Jio 5G, IDBI Bank, Kotak Bank, IDFC First Bank and others) and won a ==₹27 cr cybersecurity order==. Banks bring 56% of revenue, and Oct–Dec is usually a ==strong quarter for bank IT spending==. It is expanding into managed services and public-sector deals. Watch: dependence on bank budgets.

ARIES.text: Specialty plant-nutrient maker (chelated micronutrients, 134 brands); it pioneered chelation technology in India. Oct–Dec covers ==rabi sowing==, a key season for micronutrient demand. The Sep-quarter results on ==13 Nov 2026== will show how kharif demand and margins went, the best clue for the next quarter. Watch: weather, raw-material (fertiliser input) prices and delays in subsidy payments.

AVTNPL.text: Makes plant-based extracts and natural ingredients (A.V. Thomas Group) for food, beverage, animal-nutrition and nutraceutical customers, largely exported. ==Five quarters of rising sales== show strong demand for natural ingredients. The Sep-quarter results on ==11 Nov 2026== will confirm the trend. Watch: crop and raw-material prices, currency moves and dependence on a few export customers.

ESCONET.text: IT-infrastructure, high-performance computing (HPC) and AI-server integrator with its own ==HexaData server brand== (Red Hat certified), partnering Nvidia, Dell, AMD and Intel. Demand is coming from ==AI & HPC computing== and government digitisation: a ==₹25.7 cr C-DAC Pune hardware order== (Jul 2026), after a ₹20 cr, 340-server order from Info Edge. Its ==Singapore subsidiary is now about 31% of revenue==, a new market. ZeaCloud subsidiary is applying for ==MeitY empanelment as a sovereign government cloud== in H2 FY27; management sees a 2–3 year growth runway. Watch: thin margins on hardware resale.

GANDHAR.text: Specialty oils maker (white oils, petroleum jelly, transformer oils, lubricants) for personal-care, pharma, power and auto customers. Profit jumped on a ==much wider margin spread (₹388 vs ₹130 per kl)== and ==record revenue (+73%)==, with robust demand across industrial segments; CRISIL reaffirmed A+ and raised bank limits. Watch: margins depend on crude/base-oil spreads, which can reverse; receivables nearly doubled to ₹1,339 cr; one-time flood loss at the Silvassa unit.

TATVA.text: Specialty chemicals maker: phase-transfer catalysts, ==structure-directing agents (SDAs) for Euro 7 emission catalysts==, battery electrolyte salts, agro and pharma intermediates. Q2 was its ==highest-ever quarter==. Drivers: SDA demand from Euro 7 norms, ==electrolyte salts moving to commercial scale==, new agrochemical products and a first pharma product; ==5 semiconductor chemicals in customer qualification==. Watch: solvent prices (+60–100%) and freight (+100%) hurt Q2; management expects both to normalise in Q3.

PRIZOR.text: Gujarat-based CCTV and AI-camera brand (Prizor Plus: face recognition, number-plate reading, speed detection), plus smart TVs and classroom touch panels, sold through 9,000+ dealers. Catalyst: ==BIS-ER certification (Jan 2026)== opens government orders, and the ==April 2026 ban on non-compliant IP cameras== could shift ₹6,000–8,000 cr of yearly demand to certified makers. ==Plant runs at only 15–20% of its 50 lakh-unit capacity==, so growth needs little new investment; new Kolkata branch; raised ₹119 cr. Watch: competition from large CCTV brands.

BHAGERIA.text: Dyes and dye-intermediates maker (plus a solar power business). Q2 revenue more than doubled to ₹450 cr and EBITDA margin rose to 18% on ==higher realisations in key chemical products== and better cost absorption at higher volumes. Watch: dye-intermediate prices are cyclical; raw-material costs and export demand (trade policy, currency) can swing margins quickly.

WSTCSTPAPR.text: Paper and paperboard maker that also makes ==optical fibre and fibre-optic cables==. The board approved a ==₹290 cr optical-fibre expansion== (4.0 mn fkm of fibre and 3.1 mn fkm of cable a year, ready by Q3 FY29), nearly doubling that business on telecom and data-centre fibre demand. Watch: paper prices, wood and pulp costs, and cheap paper imports.

NITINSPIN.text: Cotton yarn and fabric maker; ==68% of sales are exports==. Q2 margins jumped on ==higher yarn prices== and full capacity use, with ==record fabric revenue== (woven sales 11.8 mn m vs 8.3 mn). Catalyst: a new ==35 mn metre/year greige fabric plant is starting up== (trial output already), so more of its own yarn becomes higher-value fabric; management cites ==favourable trade policies==. Watch: borrowings doubled to ₹1,183 cr for the expansion; cotton prices.

DPABHUSHAN.text: Gold and diamond jewellery retailer with 14 showrooms in Central India. ==Navratri moved from September (last year) to October this year==, so festive and wedding sales shift into Oct–Dec: management expects Q3 FY27 to be its ==highest-ever quarter==. ==3 new showrooms== in FY27 (Dhar, Dahod, Jabalpur, opened 30 Oct), 3–4 more by March 2027, plus a new e-commerce app. Watch: sharp gold-price swings can slow buying.

504240.text: Cables and wires maker that also does ==power EPC== and railway and telecom work. Order book ==₹471.5 cr (1.4× quarterly revenue)==, 87% of it higher-margin EPC; EPC revenue +68% and telecom +100% in H1. Catalyst: executing this EPC order book over the coming quarters. Watch: copper and aluminium prices (material cost +71%); no project timelines disclosed.

VRLLOG.text: India's largest part-load (LTL) road transporter. ==Freight rates raised about 9% this year== (April and May), lifting EBITDA margin to 23%; ==67 new branches in H1==, expanding into UP, Bihar and West Bengal. Management targets ==9–10% tonnage growth== in H2. Debt is falling and a buyback is coming. Watch: diesel and toll costs; a big diesel price cut could force rate cuts.

STOVEKRAFT.text: Kitchen appliances and cookware maker (Pigeon, Gilma). Catalysts: ==Pigeon value range and retail expansion==, ==Gilma relaunched as a premium brand==, strong e-commerce and general-trade growth, a growing own exclusive-store network, and ==festive demand in Oct–Dec==; integrated manufacturing supports margins. Watch: metal and raw-material inflation, and competition.

WHEELS.text: Steel and alloy wheel maker for trucks, tractors, cars and construction equipment, plus industrial components (wind, hydraulics). Automotive profit ==+70%== on strong demand; ==₹400–450 cr capex in FY27== for steel wheels, ==cast alloy wheels==, construction and mining wheels, air suspension and large machining. Watch: industrial-segment profit fell 34%; free cash flow is negative during the capex; steel prices.

SAHASRA.text: Electronics maker (memory modules, microSD cards, LED and EMS work) that is moving into ==semiconductor packaging==: about ₹350 cr planned over three years for one of India's first chip-packaging units. It has begun ==exporting Made-in-India microSD cards== (partnership with Germany's HAMA). Growth comes from India's electronics and chip localisation push. Watch: big capex for its size; Sep-quarter results not yet on Screener.

RAPIDFLEET.text: Transport and fleet-deployment services company. Has ==₹230 cr of FY27 orders across five sectors==, including ==₹53 cr from renewable-energy logistics== (wind/solar equipment moving), a new and growing line. Added 25 vehicles (₹12.35 cr capex), taking the fleet ==above 300==; Q1 FY27 revenue +63%. Watch: Sep-quarter results not yet on Screener; customer concentration and diesel costs.

SHREEPUSHK.text: Dye-intermediates, chemicals and fertiliser (SSP, soil conditioner) maker. Chemical sales ==+86% to ₹245 cr== despite lower volume, meaning ==much higher value per tonne== (better prices or product mix); fertiliser sales +27% with volume +9%. New ==₹70 cr Ratnagiri plant== approved (commissioning by March 2028), part of a 69,000 TPA capacity roadmap, partly funded by warrants. Watch: receivables jumped to ₹332 cr and H1 operating cash flow was negative.

THEJO.text: Wear-protection, conveyor and bulk-material-handling solutions for mining, cement, steel and ports, with subsidiaries in ==Australia and Brazil==. Growth comes from ==mining, cement and steel capex cycles== and execution of its order backlog; won a ==Vale Brazil order== (July 2026). Q1 FY27 revenue +32%, margin 14.2%. Watch: rubber and steel prices; overseas project delays; Sep-quarter results not yet on Screener.

CEIGALL.text: Road, highway and specialised EPC contractor (elevated roads, bridges, tunnels). ==Order book about ₹18,500 cr== (roughly 5× yearly revenue); new wins include a ==₹981 cr NHAI project== and a ₹705 cr border road in Arunachal; FY27 order-inflow target ₹6,000 cr. Management ==raised FY27 revenue growth guidance to 15%+==. Watch: margin guidance is conservative (11–12.5%) because of the monsoon; working capital in HAM projects.

AYMSYNTEX.text: Synthetic yarn maker (polyester and nylon filament, carpet and industrial yarns) for textiles, floor coverings and automotive fabrics. Q2 revenue ==+29% to ₹450 cr== on ==higher capacity utilisation== and steady demand for specialty filament yarns. Watch: polymer (PTA/MEG, nylon chips) price swings must be passed on to protect margins; export demand and currency.

YASHO.text: Specialty chemicals maker (rubber chemicals, lubricant additives, aroma chemicals), with a large new plant ramping up. ==Exports more than doubled==; volumes +42% in Q1 with utilisation above 65%. Catalyst: a ==15-year lubricant-additive supply deal with an MNC== (trial production Q4 FY27, commercial Q1 FY28). Management ==raised FY27 capex to ₹250 cr== and its ==FY28 revenue target to above ₹1,600 cr==. Watch: new borrowings for capex; Kacholia-backed stock can be volatile.

SHUKRAPHAR.text: Renamed ==Shukra Medtech==: pharma formulations, medical technology and analytical testing. Revenue jumped about 7× (₹44 cr in Q2) because ==export customers now drive most of the growth==; the ==MedTech arm (₹12.5 cr in Q2)== is management's top priority and will take a few quarters to scale. Watch: management itself says exports are new and must become repeatable; higher inventory and receivables.

NRAIL.text: Duplex board and paper maker (packaging board for FMCG, pharma and industrial cartons). ==Duplex-board capacity raised from 725 to 900 tonnes a day== (total about 5 lakh tonnes a year); the new lines are ramping up. Q2 revenue ==+28% to ₹670 cr== on volume growth and steady packaging demand; ICRA reaffirmed its ratings. Watch: waste-paper and imported-pulp prices, energy costs and regional competition.

ANTELOPUS.text: Oil and gas producer (Cambay basin, KG onshore). Production about ==2,000 barrels/day in October== (FY26 exit 1,758); targets ==2,500 by end-FY27, 3,500 by FY28 and 5,000 by FY29==. Seven new Karjisan wells this year (one starting soon), Bakrol fracking campaign complete, and ==seven newly acquired KG discoveries== to develop. Debt-free, about 71% EBITDA margin. Watch: crude prices, well results and KG costs (about $10 mn a well).

XPROINDIA.text: Maker of dielectric (capacitor) BOPP films and packaging films; ==meets about a third of Indian demand==, the rest is imported. ==New Barjora line (March 2026) doubled film capacity to about 8,000 tonnes a year== and is ramping up; a ==second line in the UAE starts this year==. Demand from capacitors for power grids, renewables, data centres and EV electronics; import substitution and exports to the US and Europe. Watch: debt of about ₹289 cr and ramp-up speed.

LRRPL.text: Rubber recycler turning scrap tyres into reclaimed rubber and crumb for tyre and rubber-goods makers. ==H1 FY27 revenue +65% to ₹36 cr, PAT +223% to ₹3.2 cr==, with EBITDA margin near ==16%==. Growth is driven by more tyre-maker demand for recycled rubber (green-content push) and fuller use of the new capacity; management plans further capacity-led growth. Watch: small size, scrap-tyre price swings, and customer concentration in tyre companies.

ASIANENE.text: Oilfield and mineral services company. ==Order book about ₹1,633 cr== (oil & gas 59%, mining 41%), including ==its first order outside Coal India (GSECL Ukai)==. ==H1 revenue +148% to ₹538 cr, PAT ₹29.8 cr==. Management targets ==about ₹3,000 cr revenue and ₹700 cr EBITDA by FY29/30==. More coal-handling and mine-development contracts give multi-year work. Watch: business is weighted to H2, and Kuiper operations were disrupted.

OBSCP.text: Forging and stamping maker moving from auto into exports, marine and defence. ==Exports +173% to ₹49 cr==; ==non-auto revenue more than doubled==. ==Order book above ₹1,200 cr== (55% exports, 5–6 year life). Got ==AS9100D aerospace certification== and an ==₹8.9 cr Elbit fuze order==. Spare forging capacity and new land support further growth. Watch: working capital rose 69%.

AEROFLEX.text: Stainless-steel flexible hose and assemblies maker. ==Q2 income +87% to ₹208 cr, PAT +157% to ₹36.6 cr==. ==SS hose capacity raised to 20 mn metres a year== and ==liquid-cooling skid assemblies to 12,000 a year==, aimed at ==AI data-centre cooling demand==. Management targets about 35% growth in FY27. Merging the Hyd-Air subsidiary simplifies the group. Watch: nickel/steel price swings and export demand.

KRISHNADEF.text: Defence and naval materials maker. ==Q2 revenue +56% to ₹75 cr== with a ==record 26.9% EBITDA margin==. ==Order book ₹109 cr; tender pipeline ₹305 cr==. New products: ammunition components (MoU), ==barrier exports to Belgium==, underwater welding consumables (iDEX), and the ==JAYA autonomous underwater vehicle== with Navy ISR/ASW development contracts; a Chennai AUV test facility is coming. Watch: lumpy defence orders and small order book vs pipeline.

544501.text: Power transmission & distribution EPC (substations, smart grid) plus solar. ==Order book ₹1,067 cr==, about ==3.5× FY26 revenue==. ==Seven Q2 orders worth ₹395 cr, all outside Bihar== – Bihar's share fell to ==55% from 82%==. ==H1 revenue +73% to ₹213 cr; Q2 PAT +108%==. A 3-year Odisha maintenance contract (~₹60 cr a year) started 1 Oct; tender pipeline ~₹19,150 cr. Watch: debt rising to ~₹240 cr, cash burn while growing, revenue weighted to H2.

SHAILY.text: Precision plastic parts maker; healthcare (drug-delivery pens) is now the main engine. ==Q2 standalone revenue +31% to ₹310 cr, PAT +63% to ₹67 cr==. In Q1, ==healthcare revenue rose 85% and became 51% of sales==, driven by ==GLP-1 (weight-loss) injector pen components==; pen capacity was being ==doubled from 40 mn to 80 mn units==. Industrial +25%. Watch: consumer business weak (Europe/US), oral GLP-1 tablets, client approval delays.

TAMBOLIIN.text: Investment-casting maker for pumps, valves, pneumatics, auto and aerospace, exporting to 27+ countries. ==Q2 income +20%, PAT +76% to ₹3.4 cr==, ==EBITDA margin up to 25% from 20%==. ==Fortune-100 OEM programme: 50+ parts, potential ₹20 cr+ yearly revenue== over 2–3 years; first development orders received. Adding CNC machining capacity, full use expected by FY28. Watch: OEM approvals timing and Europe demand.

MACPOWER.text: CNC machine-tool maker. ==Q2 revenue +40% to ₹120 cr, PAT +44%==. ==Demand exceeds supply== – it refunds 10–20 machine orders a month due to delivery delays; expects ==2,300–2,400 machines this year==. High-margin ==NEXA range is ~40% of orders== (target 50%). ==New 13-acre plant (+2,500 machines) from about Q2 FY28==; price hikes planned after Q3. Defence orders being executed. Watch: big capacity jump only from FY29, plant timing.

KANPRPLA.text: FIBC (jumbo bag) and woven packaging exporter. ==Q2 revenue +42% to ₹235 cr, PAT more than doubled (+114%)==. New growth legs: ==non-woven fabric line (from Nov 2026, ₹100–120 cr revenue over FY27–28)==, ==yarn capacity 7,000→10,000 t==, and ==FIBC capacity rising to 24,000 t==; Essegomma JV adds ₹10–12 cr next year. FIBC volume growth guided 5–10% this year, ~20% next. Watch: high polymer prices, freight costs, flat order book.

TEAMTECH.text: Maker and renter of construction formwork (aluminium/steel shuttering) for builders and infra contractors; listed on NSE Emerge in May 2026. ==Targets ₹140 cr revenue by FY28 on capacity expansion== funded by the IPO. Won a ==₹9.44 cr Lloyds formwork order== (more than 10% of last year's revenue), executed within 90 days. Demand comes from housing and infra building. Watch: small size, lumpy orders, and reported numbers need checking against filings.
